seen_animation: A side-view butterfly with closed upright wings (one lobed wing outline, curled antennae, a thin segmented abdomen with tick marks) sits on the tip of a grey-outlined finger of a hand. In frame 1 it is right of center with the wing tilted toward the right and the abdomen angled steeply down-right. In frames 2-4 it moves up and to the left while the wing rotates to stand upright and the abdomen levels out to near horizontal. From frame 5 to frame 12 it stays near the left-center of the frame with only small drifts and slight wing tilt changes. In frame 13 it shifts a little further left and holds there through frame 16. The grey hand outline moves with it; its outline changes shape noticeably between frames 1 and 2 and again around frames 9-10, where an extra lobe appears on the left.
seen_film: A monarch butterfly with closed wings is perched on the tip of a finger of a hand lit against a black background. In frames 1-4 the hand and butterfly move up and to the left while the wings rotate from leaning right to standing more upright. Frames 5-12 hold roughly in place, with small wing tilts. Between frames 12 and 13 the hand and butterfly shift further left and down, the lighting changes, and the wings turn so that the orange underside faces the camera. They hold in that position through frame 16.
named_subject: A butterfly with closed wings perched on a fingertip
evidence: Frames 1-4 in both show the butterfly moving up-left while the wing rotates from leaning right to upright (animation frame 1 has the abdomen angled steeply down-right and the wing tilted right, matching film frame 1; by frame 4 both are upright). Frames 5-12 in both hold near left-center with small tilts. In frame 13 both shift left and hold through frame 16. The butterfly is at matching positions on the finger in every frame. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The film's wing turn at frames 13-16, where the wings swing to show their underside, is only shown as a small left shift in the animation, and the grey hand outline is redrawn with a different shape between frames 1-2 and 9-10.
closes_when: In frames 13-16 the wing outline visibly rotates or widens toward the viewer as it does in the film, and the grey hand keeps the same outline shape from frame to frame, only translating, from frame 1 to frame 2 and through frames 9-10.
protect: The matched path and timing (up-left travel in 1-4, hold in 5-12, left shift at 13); the butterfly's placement on the fingertip in every frame; the doodle's lobed wing outline, curled antennae and tick-marked abdomen; a single stable black character drawing without redraws.
identity_gap: The character is the doodle's lobed wing, curled antennae and tick-marked abdomen seen from the side with wings closed; the short doubled line along the wing's leading edge (visible in frames 4, 5, 13, 16) is close to the doodle's own double-line habit but is slightly heavier than the doodle uses there.
